summary: The existing provider lifecycle and tenant-aware repository can host semantics, but several contracts are currently SQL/string-oriented. The highest risks are identity propagation, cache isolation, datasource governance, parameter binding, and compatibility with existing dry-run consumers.

suggestions.title: Resolve semantic type and datasource before provider construction
suggestions.rationale: `QueryModel.provider` defaults to `db`, while `Connection.get_provider()` dispatches solely from `entry.provider`; a `kind: semantic` nested inside `query_raw` will otherwise reach the normal DB provider. Resolve and validate the semantic resource first, then return both the semantic provider and the actual datasource/driver metadata so later PBAC checks do not authorize the literal provider name `semantic`.

suggestions.title: Propagate principal identity into semantic compilation and MultiQS children
suggestions.rationale: `AbstractQuery` stores `_principal`, but `QS.build_provider()` does not pass it to providers. MultiQS local execution constructs `QueryObject` without a principal, so request-less AI-agent calls and child semantic slugs cannot reliably produce `QSPrincipal.to_userinfo()` for RLS or metric authorization.

suggestions.title: Key caches by compiled parameters, identity, and external model content
suggestions.rationale: `BaseProvider.checksum()` hashes only `_query`, while `result_cache_key()` also depends on the persisted definition revision. A parameterized `CompiledQuery` can therefore collide across filter or user values, and a directory-backed model can change without changing the DB revision. Cache parsed models by content digest and compiled/results by canonical request, dialect, user attributes, SQL parameters, and resolved file digest.

suggestions.title: Define how CompiledQuery parameters reach asyncdb
suggestions.rationale: The proposed result contains `sql` and `parameters`, but the existing execution path calls `conn.query(self._query)` with no parameter arguments. The semantic provider must either use a verified driver-specific binding API or deliberately render safe literals; silently dropping parameters would produce incorrect results and undermine the filter-safety contract.

suggestions.title: Normalize and reject transport conditions before semantic validation
suggestions.rationale: `QueryService` merges JSON and query parameters into one conditions dictionary, and `QS` forwards that dictionary to the provider. Semantic request parsing should explicitly allow only metrics, dimensions, filters, time grain, limit, and documented options; it must strip or reject transport controls such as query formatting and filenames, define body-versus-query precedence, and enforce bounded limits.

suggestions.title: Make the catalog endpoint tenant-aware and field-redacting
suggestions.rationale: Existing describe routes resolve tenant stores and perform slug visibility checks, but the current `ResourceType` shim has no `SEMANTIC` member and no existing field-level catalog response. The new endpoint must authenticate the slug, resolve the correct tenant store, apply metric/dimension decisions before serializing names or definitions, and avoid exposing unauthorized catalog metadata.

suggestions.title: Preserve the legacy dry_run tuple while exposing the object result separately
suggestions.rationale: `QS.dry_run()` unpacks provider output as `(result, error)`, and `QueryService.test_slug()` treats `result` as a string for replacement and EXPLAIN. Returning `CompiledQuery` directly from that path would break existing consumers. Keep the established tuple contract and add a semantic compile method or an explicit adapter from `CompiledQuery` to the legacy dry-run representation.

suggestions.title: Make policy layers conjunctive and preserve fail-closed error semantics
suggestions.rationale: `enforce_principal()` is the existing PBAC gate and intentionally no-ops when PBAC is disabled, while secured semantic models must still deny by default. Define that resource PBAC, per-field PBAC, model `SecurityPolicy`, and YAML `row_filters` are all required constraints; semantic validation failures should use the existing 4xx exception taxonomy rather than being wrapped as generic 500 errors by `QS.build_provider()`.

suggestions.title: Constrain directory-backed model paths and hash resolved bytes
suggestions.rationale: A relative model path is untrusted resource data. Resolve it beneath the configured directory, reject traversal and escapes (including symlink escapes if unsupported), cap file size, and parse with safe YAML loading. The loader must hash the actual resolved bytes so path-backed revisions cannot bypass compilation and result-cache invalidation.

suggestions.title: Keep the optional compiler dependency behind the existing lazy provider boundary
suggestions.rationale: `Connection.load_provider()` already imports providers dynamically and `querysource.providers` exposes only `BaseProvider`; mirror that boundary for Sidemantic so importing QuerySource without `querysource[semantic]` remains functional. Add tests using the existing fake repository to verify a clear configuration error, no DuckDB execution, and no warehouse connection during model loading.

suggestions.title: Use an explicit dialect registry rather than inferring from class names alone
suggestions.rationale: `SUPPORTED` is a registry of driver classes, but the driver base contracts do not expose a canonical SQL dialect. Add a maintained driver-to-Sidemantic dialect table with explicit aliases, unsupported-driver behavior, and warning tests; otherwise datasource names and asyncdb driver names can silently compile for the wrong warehouse.

suggestions.title: Test semantic behavior through every existing execution surface
suggestions.rationale: The repository has distinct slug, direct `QS`, tenant, describe, and MultiQS paths, with separate request and principal authorization behavior. The acceptance suite should cover inline and path models, missing optional dependency, invalid filters, unknown fields, parameter binding, RLS differences between principals, tenant isolation, cache invalidation, catalog redaction, and legacy dry-run compatibility.
